newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 26.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Czech and Slovak Customs Union met yesterday to discuss a number of problems, none of which were satisfactorily solved. "We sense much more cauition on the Slovak government's side regarding the protection of their domestic market," Trade and Industry Minister, Vladimir Dlouhy, stated.

- President Vaclav Havel was taken to hospital yesterday with pneumonia. Havel has been sick for the last two weeks and was hospitalised because his ilness had not improved. Havel has been forced to cancel some foreign visits due to his health.

- Production at Kralupy's refinery should be enough to meet the country's fuel demands, according to a spokesman for Ceska Rafinerska, Ales Soukup. The capacity of the company's refinery in Litvinov was reduced following a weekend fire, the causes of which have not yet been identified. Soukup does not expect that it will be necessary to utilise state fuel reserves.
- There are currently orders for 10,000 Skoda Octavias, though the plant expects to be able to fill about half of these orders by the end of the year.
- The investment bank which will arrange the sale of Agrobanka to a strategic investor should be chosen today. Agrobanka was placed under forced administration in September.

- According to a survey of businesses involved in foreign trade, these businesses remain pessimistic about the development of the foreign trade deficit, expecting the deficit to increase to 162 billion crowns by the end of the year.

- Small and medium-sized firms used 1.1 billion crowns in the first nine months of this year from a program to support these businesses. Some 180 million crowns remains to be used by new applicants to the end of the year.
- ZPS group expects turnover to increase to 5.5 billion crowns by the end of the year, compared to last year's 4.15 billion crowns. Gross profit is expected to reach 260 million crowns.
- Skoda Liaz is planning to begin manufacturing lorries abroad in the coming year. The company expects to open plants in Poland, Brazil, and Bulgaria.
- Stavby Silnic a Zeleznic a.s. posted turnover of 4.3 billion crowns by the end of October which exceeds the results for all of last year.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Czech Railways wants to solve its deepening financial problems by increasing fares for foreign travellers by up to five times starting next June.
- Exporting agricultural products to the European Union will become easier as of next year, according to Agriculture Minister, Josef Lux.
PRAVO - Ceska Posta will most likely increase its rates starting April 1, 1997, according to Zdenek Krulis from the Ministry of Transportation and Telecommunications.
